investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official home page and '/programmation' page. The venue's own home page carries a NightClub JSON-LD block with its own GEO coordinates; the programmation page (a Next.js app) already streams its full event list as a first-party embedded 'events' JSON array inside its initial HTML response (a React Server Component 'self.__next_f.push' payload) — no separate client-side request needed. No escalation was required.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://la-java.fr/programmation returned this venue's own Next.js page. Its initial HTML already embeds a first-party JSON array (19 events at the time of retrieval) inside a React Server Component 'self.__next_f.push' script chunk — each event carrying its own stable id, name, a full ISO datetime, type, poster, and outbound ticketUrl. A second, independent fetch minutes later (research/source-investigations/la-java-paris-01/evidence/programmation-raw-refetch.html) reproduced the exact same 19 records byte-for-byte, empirically confirming id stability. This fully answered the investigation question at Level 1; no escalation was needed.

venue_reference: La Java (historic Latin/world-music-leaning concert club, 105 rue du Faubourg du Temple, 75010 Paris)

identity.notes: The retained home page's own embedded schema.org JSON-LD directly states '@type":"NightClub","name":"La Java"' with 'address':{'streetAddress':'105 rue du Faubourg du Temple','postalCode':'75010'} and 'sameAs' links to the venue's own verified Instagram/Facebook/TikTok handles ('la_java_paris'/'lajava.paris') — a self-consistent, first-party retained artifact at the venue's own domain la-java.fr, matching the assigned venue address exactly. Public sources (Wikipedia, ABC Salles) independently corroborate this as the historic club operating at this address since 1923, used here only as a discovery lead, not as fact authority.

site_classification.platform: Next.js (App Router / React Server Components). The '/programmation' page's own initial HTML response embeds its full event list as a first-party JSON array inside one of several '<script>self.__next_f.push([1,"..."])</script>' React Flight-protocol chunks — the unescaped string content of one such chunk contains a bracket-balanced '"events":[...]' array. This is a distinct streaming-data convention from ingestion/sveltekit-data/ (a different framework's own '__data.json' shape). Ticket purchase redirects to a third-party ticketing domain (shotgun.live), but the venue's own page directly and consistently designates which Shotgun URL belongs to which event — that designation itself is first-party.

title.notes: Each embedded event object's own 'name' field, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each embedded event object's own 'date' field's date portion (e.g. '2026-08-28T17:30:00.000Z'), stated directly. The calendar-date portion is safe to use as-is regardless of the timezone-labelling issue noted under 'time' below, since no cross-midnight shift is plausible for this source's own evening/night event times.

time.value: 17:30 (Europe/Paris, FLOATING_LOCAL — the source's own trailing '.000Z' is NOT a genuine UTC instant)
time.notes: Each embedded event object's own 'date' field's time-of-day portion is directly stated, but its trailing '.000Z' is honestly NOT treated as a confirmed UTC instant: this investigation cross-checked the SAME retained page's own human-readable card text for another event ('jeu. 27 août, 21:00', for event id '2026-08-23-java-party', whose JSON 'date' is '2026-08-27T21:00:00.000Z') — the digits are identical with no timezone conversion applied. A genuine UTC->Europe/Paris (UTC+2 in August) conversion would have shown '23:00', not '21:00'. Recorded as FLOATING_LOCAL, matching the same honest distinction already established for tempodrom-berlin-01.

end.notes: No end-time or end-date field exists anywhere in the embedded event objects.

venue_location.notes: Single-venue source. The home page's own NightClub JSON-LD directly states both the full postal address AND its own 'geo':{'latitude':48.8714,'longitude':2.3702} GEO property — a first-party, directly-evidenced coordinate pair, not geocoder-derived (location_status should be recorded CONFIRMED, not merely GEOCODED, per this project's coordinate-provenance convention already used for uber-arena-berlin-01).

source_record_id.notes: Each embedded event object's own 'id' field. Stability empirically proven: a second, independent fetch of the same page minutes later (ev-programmation-refetch-html) reproduced every one of the 19 records' 'id' values, and every other field, byte-for-byte identically — satisfying the stable-identifier rule's 'proven empirically' path.

event_url.notes: Each embedded event object's own 'ticketUrl' field, stated directly — this is the venue's own first-party-authored designation of where to buy tickets for that specific event, even though the URL itself resolves to a third-party ticketing domain (Shotgun). The designation (which URL belongs to which event) is first-party; the checkout page's own content is not used as evidence for anything here.

price.notes: No price field exists in the embedded event objects. Price, where shown at all, would only appear on the third-party Shotgun checkout page, which this policy does not treat as first-party price authority.
